WITH status AS (
  SELECT 
    a.artregistry, 
    a.artname, 
    a.mattype, 
    s.lightsensitivity, 
    l.lightlux, 
    CASE 
      WHEN l.lightlux > s.lightsensitivity THEN 'Over Exposure' 
      ELSE 'Within Limits' 
    END AS status 
  FROM 
    artifactscore AS a 
    JOIN sensitivitydata AS s ON a.artregistry = s.artref 
    JOIN conditionassessments AS c ON a.artregistry = c.artrefexamined 
    JOIN lightandradiationreadings AS l ON c.lightreadrefobserved = l.lightradregistry
) 
SELECT 
  artregistry, 
  artname, 
  mattype, 
  lightsensitivity, 
  status 
FROM 
  status;

parts.name: get_all_knowledge_definitions

parts.text:
Here is a table containing all sensitive artifacts, along with their registry number, name, material type, light sensitivity, and current status.

| Registry Number | Name | Material Type | Light Sensitivity | Current Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ART54317 | Culture Painting | Stone | High | Within Limits |
| ART54254 | Poor Vase | Textile | Low | Within Limits |
| ART69978 | Order Painting | Bronze | High | Over Exposure |

The current status is determined by comparing the light sensitivity of the artifact with the current light levels. If the current light level is above the safe light levels for the artifact, it is considered 'Over Exposure'; otherwise, it is 'Within Limits'.

The safe light levels are determined by the light sensitivity of the artifact:
- High sensitivity artifacts (textiles, paper) must not exceed 50 lux
- Medium sensitivity (paintings, wood) must not exceed 200 lux
- Low sensitivity (stone, metal) can tolerate up to 300 lux
